The diff nevertheless calls `useCanvasFocusRelease()` and adds `data-canvas-toolbar=""` in `board-toolbar.tsx`, changing keyboard behaviour on a second, unverified surface (board also has its own sticky-color `onCloseAutoFocus` focus choreography at board-toolbar.tsx:126-130).

samples.summary: The design doc added in this same change contradicts the code it documents: `docs/design/slides/slides-keyboard-shortcuts.md:141-165` says the hook is "called by the desktop slides toolbar" and that "the board toolbar can adopt the hook when that surface is verified" — but this diff already adopts it in the board toolbar. The canonical doc therefore records behaviour that is false as of this commit (nested design docs are not link/consistency-checked by CI, so nothing else catches it).

Board adoption conflicts with a documented board design decision. `packages/frontend/src/app/board/is-editable-target.ts:6-13` states the BUTTON branch exists specifically "so Space on a focused `BoardToolbar` toggle still activates the button instead of entering pan mode". Blurring toolbar buttons to `document.body` after every pointer-driven click means the next Space now enters board pan mode rather than re-activating the just-used toggle — a behaviour change to board pan-mode that no doc under `docs/design/board/` records.

Overlapping focus-release mechanisms are now left side by side: the pre-existing per-palette `useMenuCloseHandlers(releaseFocusToBody)` pattern (`shape-controls.tsx:60`, `border-picker.tsx:72`, `text-element-controls.tsx:62`, `table-controls.tsx:103`, `gradient-editor.tsx:307`) exists solely to drop focus off slides toolbar triggers, which the new global hook also does. Neither the doc nor the diff says which is canonical or whether the per-palette wiring should be retired, so future toolbar controls have two competing conventions.

`CANVAS_TOOLBAR_ATTR` is exported as the single source of truth for the opt-in attribute but no call site imports it — both toolbars hardcode `data-canvas-toolbar=""` (with the module comment excusing this). The constant is therefore an unused export (also a knip risk) and the coupling it claims to centralise is only enforced by comments.

Approach-fit: the root cause is the over-broad `<button>` branch of `isEditableTarget` in `packages/slides/src/view/editor/interactions/keyboard.ts`, and the chosen remedy is three document-level capture listeners plus heuristics (pointer-driven flag, popup-open detection, keepalive exemption, deferred re-read of `activeElement`) living in the frontend layer. The task doc rules out touching `isEditableTarget`, so this is within the sanctioned approach, but the heuristic surface is notably larger than the defect and is now duplicated in behaviour expectations across two editors.

`useCanvasFocusRelease()` is called unconditionally in `SlidesToolbar` even though the mobile branch returns `MobileSlidesToolbar` (explicitly out of scope per the task doc) and never renders a `data-canvas-toolbar` root — installing three document listeners with nothing to act on.

verdict.reason: The doc text is present as described and is contradicted by the code it documents. docs/design/slides/slides-keyboard-shortcuts.md:142-146 describes useCanvasFocusRelease() as "called by the desktop slides toolbar", and lines 162-165 say "the attribute is opt-in, so the board toolbar can adopt the hook when that surface is verified" — framing board adoption as future work. But packages/frontend/src/app/board/board-toolbar.tsx:5 imports the hook, :132-137 calls it (with a comment saying the board opts in "exactly as SlidesToolbar does"), and :186 renders <Toolbar data-canvas-toolbar="">. So board adoption is already done in this commit and the canonical design doc records false, stale behaviour for the subsystem it owns. This is design-doc discipline (canonical doc must match the shipped architecture), a factual contradiction rather than a wording preference, so it is major in kind. No guard, follow-up note, or other doc text reconciles the discrepancy.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described. `is-editable-target.ts:6-13` records the BUTTON branch's rationale as keeping Space on a focused BoardToolbar toggle from entering pan mode; `board-toolbar.tsx:137,186` now opts the board toolbar into `useCanvasFocusRelease()`, which blurs releasable toolbar buttons (including pressed toggles, `toolbar-focus-release.ts:59-79,107-123` + `menu-focus.ts:68-72`) to `document.body` after pointer-driven interactions. `board-view.tsx:619-631` then treats the next Space as pan mode, since `isEditableTarget(body)` is false. Grepping `docs/design/board/*` for focus/keyboard/shortcut finds nothing recording this; the mechanism is documented only in `docs/design/slides/slides-keyboard-shortcuts.md:136-165`, which still states board adoption is pending/opt-in, and `docs/tasks/active/20260819-slides-toolbar-focus-release-todo.md:49-55` lists the board branch as explicitly out of scope. No guard or caller makes the behaviour change unreachable, and the concern (undocumented behaviour change contradicting a recorded design decision, canonical doc not updated) is within the design-fit lens.

finding.summary: Canonical design doc not updated for the new `data-text-edit-keepalive` exemption. The doc's "It deliberately does nothing when" list (lines 147-160) is the spec for this hook and is now incomplete; worse, its last bullet asserts text-edit controls are handled purely by the deferred activeElement re-read ("which is what makes text-edit controls … no-ops"), which the delta contradicts by adding an explicit keepalive special case in `toolbar-focus-release.ts:76`. CONTRIBUTING expects the behaviour change to be folded into the canonical subsystem doc.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. The code has an explicit keepalive exemption: toolbar-focus-release.ts:43 defines TEXT_EDIT_KEEPALIVE_SELECTOR = "[data-text-edit-keepalive]" and line 76 adds `el.closest(TEXT_EDIT_KEEPALIVE_SELECTOR) === null` to isReleasable(), documented as deliberate in the file comments (lines 24-26, 34-42). The canonical design doc docs/design/slides/slides-keyboard-shortcuts.md:147-160 lists only four "deliberately does nothing when" conditions and its last bullet (157-160) attributes text-edit no-ops purely to the deferred activeElement re-read — no keepalive condition. A grep for keepalive/keep-alive across all of docs/design yields exactly one unrelated hit (notifications.md:256, SSE heartbeat); no design doc anywhere mentions data-text-edit-keepalive, including slides-toolbar-redesign.md, slides-hover-and-text-edit-entry.md and docs/docs-font-controls.md. Following the chain to the only other descriptions of the hook makes it worse rather than providing a counterexample: docs/tasks/active/20260819-slides-toolbar-focus-release-todo.md:33-35 lists the guards without keepalive, and its lessons file at line 29 states "No text-edit special case was needed," which the code now contradicts; these are task docs under docs/tasks/, not the canonical subsystem doc, so they would not satisfy doc discipline even if accurate. The todo's own checked item (line 46-47) "Document the rule in docs/design/slides/slides-keyboard-shortcuts.md" is therefore no longer satisfied. Blocking under the design-fit rubric as a doc-discipline/spec-conformance gap: the behaviour change was not folded into the canonical subsystem doc, and the doc actively asserts a superseded mechanism.

The delta makes the board toolbar a second caller (`board-toolbar.tsx:137,186`) without updating either sentence, and nothing is recorded in `docs/design/board/board-editing-parity.md` either.

verdict.reason: Evidence verified verbatim. slides-keyboard-shortcuts.md:142-143 says useCanvasFocusRelease() is "called by the desktop slides toolbar", and :162-165 says board "can adopt the hook when that surface is verified" (framing board as a future adopter, with the duplicated <button> branch left in place). But board-toolbar.tsx:5,137,186 already imports the hook, calls it, and marks its root data-canvas-toolbar="", making board a present second caller — and board/is-editable-target.ts:27 still carries the duplicate BUTTON branch. The task doc (20260819-slides-toolbar-focus-release-todo.md:49-55) also explicitly lists the board surface as out of scope, so the delta contradicts it too. Grep of docs/design/board/board-editing-parity.md shows no mention of the focus-release mechanism or data-canvas-toolbar, so nothing records it elsewhere. No guard or caller makes this unreachable; the canonical subsystem design doc is now factually wrong about the architecture it governs, which is squarely the design-doc-discipline item in this lens and of major kind.
